1519045.steps: 1. On the VPN>Settings page of SonicWALL1, add a new VPN policy. Select Manual Key mode in the General tab. 2. Type a policy name in the Name field. Enter 0.0.0.0 in the IPsec Gateway Name or Address field. 3. In the Network tab, select the 'Choose local network from list' radio button under Local Networks. Select 'X0 Subnet' from the drop-down list. Select the 'Choose destination network from list' radio button under Destination Networks. Select 'Create new address object...' from the drop-down list. In the 'Add Address Object' pop-up window, enter a name 'Remote LAN'. Select VPN zone assignment. Select 'Network' type. Enter network address of the SonicWALL2 LAN. Click OK to save. 4. In the Proposals tab, enter 123 in the Incoming SPI field. Enter abc in the Outgoing SPI field. Have default settings in the Protocol, Phase 2 Encryption, and Phase 2 Authentication fields (ESP 3DES SHA1). Type 48 digits in the Encryption Key field. Type 40 digits in the Authentication Key field. Click OK to save. 5. Configure the matching VPN policy on SonicWALL2 firewall. Enter abc in the Incoming SPI field. Enter 123 in the Outgoing SPI field. Use the same values for Encryption Key and Authentication Key as in step4. 6. Send continuous ping from Host2 to Host1. Capture packets on WAN.
1519045.title: IPSec Gateway is not specified.
1519045.description:
Original ID: 5
Original Title: IPSec Gateway is not specified.
Original Description: This test verifies that encrypted traffic will go between local and remote destinations through the Manual Key VPN tunnel when IPSec Gateway is not specified on the local firewall.
1519045.result: Currently Active VPN Tunnels on the VPN>Settings page shows the active Manual Key tunnel entry as soon as the policy is created. The address shown in the Gateway column is 0.0.0.0 After ping being passed from Host2 to Host1， Packet capture shows ESP packets being sent and received on WAN IP addresses of SonicWALL1 and SonicWALL2.

1519046.title: Re-enable the Manual Key VPN policy with outgoing traffic.
1519046.description:
Original ID: 6
Original Title: Re-enable the Manual Key VPN policy with outgoing traffic.
Original Description: This test verifies that traffic will go from local to remote destination after re-enabling a Manual Key VPN policy on the local firewall.
1519046.result:
Currently Active VPN Tunnels on the VPN>Settings page shows the active Manual Key tunnel entry as soon as the policy is created. Ping is passed from Host1 to Host2. Packet capture shows ESP packets being sent and received on WAN IP addresses of SonicWALL1 and SonicWALL2.
  When the VPN policy gets disabled, the Currently Active VPN tunnels table doesn't show the Manual Key tunnel entry. Ping from Host1 is dropped. When the VPN policy gets re-enabled, the Manual Key tunnel enrty is displayed in the Currently Active VPN tunnels table and ping is passed from Host1 to Host2.
